brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Built two adjacent cells (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full) each fitted with a solid full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full). Joints locked and open faces capped. Dressed with fork in bin 0,0,0 and knife in bin 1,0,0 to demonstrate utensil storage - visible from above (polar 10).

Configurator verifies only geometry/fit and mesh clearance, not sealing or material properties. Parts are 3D-printed plastic in user-chosen material; layer lines and print settings determine water-tightness. Chose solid undrained bins (not drained variants) so shape contains contents, but no waterproof rating can be claimed or verified here.

Configurator does not verify heat resistance, food safety, chemical resistance or dishwasher durability. Those properties depend on filament choice, printer, and dishwasher temperature. No material or process can be specified here, so dishwasher safety cannot be guaranteed - never describe as dishwasher safe from this build alone.

finish.summary: Built a compact two-cell holder (2 bases + 2 solid full-depth bins, locked and capped). Each bin holds utensils (fork/knife staged on separate bin floors) to show the utensil-holder purpose. Because the Hex Cluster system is 3D-printed and only checks geometry, waterproof and dishwasher-safe claims depend on material/print choice and cannot be met by the configurator alone - solid bins help contain items but are not certified watertight or dishwasher safe.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
